$comment: P65 [[D-LINK-MACHO-IMAGE-OVERALIGNED-STATIC-IS-A-LOAD-TIME-COIN-FLIP]], the NEGATIVE half: a statically allocated object aligned more strictly than the IMAGE's own mapping granularity is refused BY NAME, never placed and shipped. $$ WHY MACH-O REFUSES WHERE ELF AND PE BOTH PLACE, and none of the three is a policy choice. An ELF PT_LOAD carries `p_align`, so [[D-LINK-ELF-IMAGE-OVERALIGNED-DATA-PLACED-AT-ALIGNED-FILE-OFFSET]] could close its load-time half by RAISING a segment's declared granularity to cover its strongest member. PE pads WITHIN the section and rides Windows' 64 KiB allocation granularity, which divides every value PE/COFF's four-bit IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_* field can encode. Mach-O's `segment_command_64` has NO alignment field at all -- `section_64.align` is read by the STATIC LINKER, never by dyld -- and every darwin image here is base-relative (MH_PIE / MH_DYLIB), so an above-page object keeps the address the linker chose and LOSES its alignment at load. $$ THE REFERENCE, Apple Silicon / macOS 26.6.2 / Apple clang 21.0.0 / ld PROJECT:ld-1267, each port probed SEPARATELY, BUILD **and** RUN, twenty runs per cell because one run decides nothing about a coin flip: x86_64 (page 4096) returns 42 at 4096, and at 8192 ld64 WARNS "reducing alignment of section __DATA,__data from 0x2000 to 0x1000 because it exceeds segment maximum alignment" and the program then returns 50/52 BY RUN; arm64 (page 16384) returns 42 twenty times out of twenty at 16384, and at 32768 draws the same warning with 0x8000 -> 0x4000 and returns 50/54 BY RUN, never 42. THE CAP TRACKS THE PAGE and the reference names it. `-Wl,-segalign,0x8000` does not lift it either: ld64 refuses the link outright with "chained fixups, page_size not 4KB or 16KB in segment #2". => No reference makes an above-page static WORK on Mach-O, so under DSS = (gcc U clang U MSVC) -- the union being over what WORKS, not what is ACCEPTED -- nothing votes to place it. DSS is one notch stricter than ld64 deliberately: ld64 warns and ships the coin flip, and a warning is not an answer where the outcome is a silent, non-deterministic miscompile. $$ THE POSITIVE HALF IS THE SAME SOURCE AT THE SAME VALUE ON THE OTHER PORT. `image.segmentPageSize` is 4096 here and 16384 on macho64-arm64-darwin-exec, so 8192 is refused here and PLACED there -- MEASURED P65, the DSS-built arm64 image returns 42 twenty times out of twenty on real Apple Silicon with dyld choosing three different slides. See examples/c/alignment_overaligned_static_placed, which carries that arm. The ceiling is a config value, and this pair is what demonstrates it. $ TWO OBJECTS BEHIND AN ODD FILLER, in both storage classes, not one: a single over-aligned static sits at its section head and is right BY LUCK -- the measurement that hid the ELF sibling for months -- so even a subject that can only be checked by a REFUSAL carries the shape a placement would need. $ NOT AN ELF OR PE ARM, and that is measured rather than conservative: this exact shape at 8192 BUILDS AND RUNS to 42 on elf64-x86_64-linux-exec and pe64-x86_64-windows-exec, so a gate on either would refuse what DSS demonstrably gets right. `positioned: false` because a link-tier diagnostic carries no source span.
